rationale.conceptual: The method uses established DFT with PBE and ONCV pseudopotentials, followed by DFPT and electron-phonon interpolation with EPW/Wannier90. It is not a textbook one-liner, as it requires understanding of electronic structure, phonon dispersion, and the Eliashberg function. However, it relies entirely on documented algorithms and open-source codes; no custom theoretical development or novel derivations needed.
rationale.execution: The pipeline involves at least five separate compute stages: SCF, band structure, optical properties (epsilon.x), phonon dispersion (ph.x), and electron-phonon coupling (EPW with Wannierization). Each stage depends on the previous and requires careful parameter choices (k-point grids, cutoffs, Wannier functions). The orchestration is fragile and demands experience with the toolchain, making it a multi-step, tool-intensive execution.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires running standard first-principles DFT workflows (Quantum ESPRESSO + EPW + Wannier90) to extract optical peaks and an electron-phonon spectral peak. The underlying method is not novel, but the multi-step pipeline requires solid domain knowledge to set up correctly. The pipeline is non-trivial but uses well-documented tools. The resource needs are moderate CPU-only DFT calculations, no GPU required.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Plane-wave DFT with 80 Ry cutoff, 24x24x8 k-points, and electron-phonon interpolation on finer grids drives moderate memory (~32 GB RAM). All calculations are CPU-only; input data is limited to pseudopotentials and lattice parameters, so data volume is negligible.
